source: captured against the installed codex-cli 0.154.0 app-server with two clients subscribed to the same thread

server_request_shape.example_reason: Allow creating <filename> with the requested touch command?

approval_request.invalid_decision_server_log: unknown variant `<other>`; the request then fails as 'approval request failed' and the tool call is rejected; the server survives

sandbox_dependence.fact: a requestApproval is only issued when the command would violate the thread's sandbox; it is not issued for every command execution
sandbox_dependence.trusted_workspace_write: when the thread cwd is a trusted project, an in-workspace write such as touch <workspace-file> executes silently with no approval request of any kind (observed with and without a native TUI attached)
sandbox_dependence.untrusted_read_only: when the thread cwd is not a trusted project, the same touch command triggers item/commandExecution/requestApproval on every subscribed connection
sandbox_dependence.implication_for_theater: approval surfacing depends on thread cwd trust and sandbox policy; a Theater control client cannot assume a tool call produces an approval request

request_params_variability.note: the exact params set depends on the command; parsers must tolerate both shapes

resolution.semantics: when one client answers, every other subscribed client receives serverRequest/resolved for that request id, so an observer can always tell the request was consumed without answering it

observer_rule: a Theater observing/control client must never send a response for an approval server request; it records the request and relies on serverRequest/resolved to learn the outcome

native_ui_retains_ownership.evidence: with a real codex TUI subscribed and a Theater-like observer also subscribed, the approval request rendered in the TUI; a single 'y' keypress in the TUI approved it; the observed command executed; the observer never sent a response

clarification.method: no server request is issued for model clarification questions
clarification.answering: the human answers by typing in the native UI, which starts a new turn; an observer only records the item
